simple.meaning: אוּד (ʼûwd) is a Hebrew word meaning “a poker (for turning or gathering embers).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אוּד (H181) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 7:4, with occurrences in Isaiah, Amos, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אוּד (H181) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אוּד (H181) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אוּד (ʼûwd) / H181 is traced through Isaiah 7:4, Amos 4:11, Zechariah 3:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

structuredEvidence.definition: a poker (for turning or gathering embers)

firstOccurrence.englishText: Tell him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don’t be afraid, neither let your heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.

timeline.evidenceText: Tell him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don’t be afraid, neither let your heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
Yahweh said to Satan, “Yahweh rebuke you, Satan! Yes, Yahweh who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Isn’t this a burning stick plucked out of the fire?”

definitions.short: a poker (for turning or gathering embers)
definitions.full: H181. ud אוּד noun masculine brand, fire-brand (originally perhaps bent stick used to stir fire) ׳א מִשְּׂרֵפָה מֻצָּל Amos 4:11 = ׳א ׳מ מֵאֵשׁ Zech 3:2 , plural הָעֲשֵׁנִים הָאוּדִים זַנְבוֺת Isa 7:4 , stumps of smoking firebrands.
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to rake together;
